UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following O R D E R 1.

The petitioner seeks enlargement on bail in FIR No.124/2021, registered under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B and 34 IPC at P.S. Barkhera, District Ratlam,
Madhya Pradesh.

2. The allegations levelled against the petitioner are that some revenue officers collided with the petitioner and his co- accused to manipulate the revenue records and mutated the farmers land in other persons name, whereupon loans were obtained from the banks on the basis of the forged records.
The specific allegation against the petitioner is that he took loan on the credit cards of the farmers from the Indusland Bank of Rs.8,80,000/-.
The petitioner was arrested on 14.10.2021 and is in custody since then.
The investigation is complete and the chargesheet has been filed.

3. In order to secure the interest of the victim farmers, vide order dated 13.05.2024, the pairokar of the petitioner was directed to file an affidavit giving details of all the immovable assets (also movable assets valuing Rs.2 lakh and above) owned by the petitioner and/or his family members on the date fixed.

4. As per the said Affidavit, the petitioner and his family are living with his parents in House No.41,
situated in village Surjana, Tehsil Taal, District Ratlam and he has 1/2/7 share in agricultural land in Khasra No.473, area 1.0100 hectare, situated in village Surjana, Tehsil Taal, District Ratlam.

5. It is directed that both the assets shall remain attached and if it is found that the petitioner was also involved in manipulating the record and victimising the innocent farmers, the State shall be at liberty to take appropriate action for disposal of the attached assets to compensate the farmers in accordance with law.
6. However, having regard to the period already spent by the petitioner in custody, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, we are inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
7. The petitioner is, accordingly, directed to be enlarged on bail on his furnishing bail bonds to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
8. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
9. As a result, the pending interlocutory application also stands disposed of.

sentences.text: In the instant case, the petitioner is also accused of taking loan on the basis of forged revenue record, which was allegedly fabricated in collusion and connivance with the revenue officers.
The petitioner had taken a loan of Rs.11,57,000/- which she is stated to have paid in entirety as can be seen from the No Dues Certificate issued by the bank.
2. Be that as it may, the arrest of the petitioner was stayed vide order dated 13.05.2024, subject to the condition that she will continue to appear before the Trial Court regularly.
3. It is not in dispute that the petitioner has joined the investigation and she undertakes to appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required.
4. Taking into consideration all the attending circumstances, the interim order dated 13.05.2024 is made absolute.

The petitioner shall remain on bail till the proceeding reaches a logical conclusion,
subject to the condition that in the event of filing of chargesheet, she will regularly appear before the Trial Court unless exemption granted in this regard.
5. The Special Leave Petition stands disposed of accordingly.
6. As a result, the pending interlocutory application stands disposed of.

(SATISH KUMAR YADAV) (PREETHI T.C.)
